newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. servicemen withdraw rape appeal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. servicemen withdraw rape appeal.

text.p: Two of the three U.S. servicemen sentenced for raping a schoolgirl in Okinawa last year have withdrawn their appeals, Kyodo news agency said on Thursday.
Marine Privates Rodrico Harp, 22, and Kendrick Ledet, 21, had appealed to Japan's Supreme Court, saying their prison terms were "too harsh" for the crime they committed.
Harp had been sentenced to seven years and Ledet to 6-1/2 years. The third person, Navy Seaman Marcus Gill, 23, who was sentenced to seven years, had not appealed.
Kyodo had no more details on the withdrawal.
The rape case became a lightning rod for criticism by local residents against the lopsided concentration of U.S. military facilities in Okinawa.

The island, some 1,000 km (625 miles) southwest of Tokyo, is home to three-quarters of the U.S. military facilities in Japan and hosts about half of the 47,000 U.S. military personnel stationed in the country, although it constitutes less than one percent of Japan's total land area.
